heading: INT. CAPE ROSS TELEGRAPH OFFICE - NIGHT - 1889

units.text: INT. CAPE ROSS TELEGRAPH OFFICE - NIGHT - 1889
A stone hut at the edge of a cliff.
A potbellied stove, a battered desk, a brass key under a green-shaded lamp.
Wind howls around the shutters.
A storm lantern swings from a hook.
CLARENCE PENHALLOW, 40s, a telegraph operator in sleeve garters and a worn waistcoat, taps the key steadily, one eye on a log book.
Beside him on a stool sits MABEL PENHALLOW, 10, his daughter, bundled in a shawl and chewing a pencil, copying out letters in a copybook.
Dash-dot-dash... dash-dash...
units.name: CLARENCE

units.text: What does it say, Papa?
units.name: MABEL

units.text: Ship in distress. Off the Skerries.
units.name: CLARENCE

units.text: Is she sinking?
units.name: MABEL

units.text: She's calling.
units.name: CLARENCE

units.text: A bell rings above the door.
Clarence picks up the telephone receiver, wired to a grey box on the wall, and holds it to his ear.
Penhallow. This is Hollingsworth at Lloyd's. Do you read me?
units.name: HOLLINGSWORTH

units.text: I read you, sir.
units.name: CLARENCE

units.text: The Admiralty has authorized the lifeboat. They want the coordinates relayed to Falmouth. Immediately.
units.name: HOLLINGSWORTH

units.text: Coordinates, sir. Fifty degrees, four minutes north. Five degrees, nineteen west.
units.name: CLARENCE

units.text: Repeat.
units.name: HOLLINGSWORTH

units.text: Fifty, four, north. Five, nineteen, west.
units.name: CLARENCE

units.text: A pause.
Static.
Good man. Stay on the wire.
units.name: HOLLINGSWORTH

units.text: Clarence hangs up and begins to tap at the key, fast, sure, fingers dancing.
Mabel watches, wide-eyed.
The wind howls.
The lantern sways.
Papa, will they be in time?
units.name: MABEL

units.text: Not if I stop to talk.
units.name: CLARENCE

units.text: Mabel nods.
Bends over her copybook.
The key chatters on into the dark.
